records.exception_reason: Foundational source included for its coarse-to-fine navigation primitives.
records.relevance_note: A primary source for how terminal agents navigate large file-systems using specialized search tools.
records.reason_included: Explicit definition of coarse-to-fine navigation as a harness-level requirement.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) must provide specialized navigation commands like 'search_dir' and 'search_file' to allow the agent to incrementally localize problems without loading full files into context.
Failures in problem localization often stem from the agent skipping 'find' steps and jumping directly to 'open_file' based on broad keyword guesses.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The repository map uses Tree-sitter to extract and rank symbols by relevance, providing the LLM with a 10kb summary of the entire project structure to guide file search.
This mechanism reduces the 'wrong file' failure mode by 2.4x compared to generic ripgrep search by providing structural context.

records.title: Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases
records.relevance_note: A paper focused on helping agents 'think before editing' specifically to avoid mis-localization in large repos.
records.reason_included: Proposes a 'reconnaissance loop' mechanism where implementation tools are locked until a localization invariant is met.

claim_snippets.claim_text: We implement a 'Localization Lock' where the agent must provide a checksum of the target file's current state before editing tools are enabled, forcing accurate identification.
The agent uses a two-pass exploration strategy: pass 1 build a dependency tree of the bug report symbols; pass 2 navigates only those tree nodes.

records.title: Codex Prompting Guide
records.relevance_note: Defines concrete search, read, batching, and truncation policies for coding agents.
records.reason_included: Directly specifies localization and exploration behavior that changes harness control logic.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The guide treats codebase exploration as one of the most critical prompt snippets to preserve when migrating a harness to codex-cli.
The recommended prompt tells the agent to prefer `rg`/`rg --files`, choose dedicated read/search tools over raw shell when available, and parallelize file searches and reads.

Exploration is prescribed as a batched loop: decide all needed reads first, issue one parallel batch, analyze results, then repeat only if new unpredictable reads arise; tool responses should be truncated to about 10k tokens with head-and-tail preservation.

records.title: Remove hard-coded output limits from gpt-5.1 (non-codex) system prompt
records.relevance_note: Shows how stale output-limit instructions distort file reading and search breadth.
records.reason_included: Concrete localization failure caused by prompt-level chunking assumptions.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports that Codex added a configurable `tool_output_token_limit`, but non-codex GPT-5.1 prompts still hard-code a 250-line / 10-kilobyte shell-reading rule.
With `tool_output_token_limit = 25000`, the model still behaves as if output is capped at roughly 256 lines / 10 KB, insists on 250-line chunking, and treats full-file reads as truncated.
The reported consequence is too many tool calls, model confusion, longer task execution, and lower-quality outputs.

records.relevance_note: Captures a concrete wrong-file failure after long multi-file editing sessions.
records.reason_included: Direct evidence for wrong-target avoidance and re-anchor requirements.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The model repeatedly sends Edit calls to a recently edited file path instead of the intended file, even while its text output names the intended target correctly.
After receiving repeated `No changes to make` errors, the model retries the identical wrong-path Edit call 15+ times without correcting the path.
The bug was observed deep in a long conversation (~40+ tool calls), where the intended MEMORY.md path was far from the project files edited earlier in the session.

records.title: Feature: glob and grep tools have no result-count limit configurable by user — on large monorepos these silently return truncated results with no warning
records.relevance_note: Shows incomplete search results can look complete to the agent in large repos.
records.reason_included: Concrete wrong-target precursor caused by tool-schema omissions and silent truncation.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports that Gemini CLI `glob` and `grep` silently truncate results on large monorepos, with no warning that the returned set is incomplete.
The reporter identifies hardcoded output caps in `ripGrep.ts` and missing `max_results` fields in the grep and glob JSON schemas, leaving the agent unable to request smaller pages or paginate.
The proposed fix is to add an optional `max_results` parameter and explicit truncation messages telling the agent to refine the pattern or page results.

records.title: [Bug]: Slow startup (several minutes) on Linux due to Ripgrep download hang
records.relevance_note: Shows tool bootstrap assumptions can block search before exploration begins.
records.reason_included: Useful environment-diagnosis failure where system `rg` exists but harness logic ignores it.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports multi-minute startup stalls because the CLI tries to download ripgrep to `~/.gemini/bin/rg` during initialization.
Installing ripgrep system-wide at `/usr/bin/rg` does not help because the CLI looks only in its internal bin directory.
Setting `"useRipgrep": false` in settings bypasses ripgrep initialization and immediately removes the startup delay.

records.title: Proposal: AGENTS.md v1.1: Making Implicit Semantics Explicit, Clarifying Scope, and Recommendation for Progressive Disclosure
records.relevance_note: Specifies how agents should discover, scope, and progressively load file-local guidance.
records.reason_included: Directly relevant to narrowing guidance to the current file region without polluting context.

claim_snippets.claim_text: AGENTS.md guidance is ancestor-scoped: only files in the target file's directory or parent directories apply, guidance accumulates down the tree, and more specific files override ancestors.
The proposal adds optional frontmatter (`description`, `tags`) so harnesses can index available AGENTS.md files and decide when to load full contents without up-front full-file loads.

The recommended progressive-disclosure flow is: scan AGENTS.md paths at session start, inject a lightweight index, then load files on demand; during compaction, preserve behavior-affecting guidance first.

records.title: CodeScout: An Effective Recipe for Reinforcement Learning of Code Search Agents
records.relevance_note: CodeScout: An Effective Recipe for Reinforcement Learning of Code Search Agents is a paper source with details on terminal only localization, localization finish schema relevant to execution control.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on execution loop, tool gateway, verification.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper frames code localization as the first step in issue resolution and reports that relying on general-purpose models for localization inside the coding loop can cause high costs, incorrect fixes, and code bloat.

CodeScout uses a bash-only scaffold with standard Unix commands such as `rg`, `find`, `ls`, `grep`, and `sed`, plus a `LocalizationFinish` tool whose structured schema improved reward-signal fidelity over brittle string outputs.

During training, agents often exhausted the step budget without submitting predictions; adding a binary reward for terminating exactly at the step limit mitigated collapse, while auxiliary rewards for parallel tool-calling hurt performance and were replaced by explicit prompting.

records.relevance_note: Measured workflow for narrowing candidate files from issue text before coding.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper studies an LLM-powered agent that improves file-level bug localization through lightweight query reformulation and summarization before retrieval.
The agent extracts key information from bug reports such as identifiers and code snippets, reformulates the query, and then orchestrates BM25 retrieval with those preprocessed fields.
Using the best reformulation technique, the agent improves first-file ranking by 35% over a BM25 baseline and file retrieval by up to 22% over SWE-agent.

records.title: Hybrid-Gym: Training Coding Agents to Generalize Across Tasks
records.relevance_note: Hybrid-Gym: Training Coding Agents to Generalize Across Tasks is a paper source with details on function localization task, issue localization task relevant to execution control.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on execution loop, tool gateway, verification.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Hybrid-Gym explicitly includes function localization and issue localization tasks so agents must search the repository, reason over descriptions or issues, and make file edits without relying on full executable setup.

The function-localization task requires effective targeted search over the whole repository, while issue localization requires analyzing the issue, exploring the repository, planning the fix, and making successful file-editing actions.

The dependency-search task forces agents to resolve each referenced name to the correct in-repo definition across files, which is non-trivial because multiple modules may share the same name; evaluation checks that all and only the correct dependency definitions are annotated.
